descriptions.text: Borough Field Guide. Ahh, look at you. The intrepid explorer. Alone. Lost. Afraid. But there is no reason to be frightened. Not today, not now. Not when the trusty field guide has added monster types to this area of the map. Now when you gaze upon the unknown, that fear is somewhat lessened. Instead of delving into the strange, mysterious dark, being devoured by an unseen horror, you will now know exactly what it is as it chews upon your tasty innards.

recap.text: Carl loots the persistent item from the boss's corpse among the crushed tusklings; Donut already has hers. The AI reads the Borough Field Guide's description in a whispery David Attenborough impression. Carl zooms his minimap out, and hovering over the far southeastern quadrant, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5, Axebeak. It covers a limited area, and one must reach the center and kill the boss to get it.

A single object appears on the map in the middle of an enormous pile of dead mimic. Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map and borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl knows what this one is: the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.

The party takes the field guide from the borough boss corpse. It shows the level and description of every mob in the entire bowl. In the dark, it shows fist-sized Night Frights coming up out of the sand dunes everywhere. They run at their prey, attach themselves and explode, like the rot stickers of the first floor.

beats.headline: An Attenborough whisper
beats.text: The crushed tusklings lie everywhere, and Carl reaches down to loot the persistent item from the boss's corpse; Donut already has hers. The AI reads its description in a whispery David Attenborough impression: Borough Field Guide. Carl zooms his minimap out, and the quadrants round the arena are outlined now. Hovering over one to the far southeast, where nobody has been, brings a tooltip through the fog of war: Mobs Level 2-5. Axebeak. Useful, but like the neighborhood map the area is limited, and one has to reach the center and kill the boss to get it.
beats.gist: Carl loots the boss's corpse and gets the Borough Field Guide, which shows mob levels in far quadrants.

Neighborhood bosses drop the neighborhood map, borough bosses the field guide, and thanks to both the cookbook and Mordecai, Carl already knows what this one will be. It is the Map of the Stars, which adds boss locations and descriptions to a large area of the map. It is a little late to be useful, but he wades into the gore and picks it up anyway.

beats.headline: The whole bowl
beats.text: The party has taken the field guide from the borough boss corpse. Now they can see the level and description of every mob in the area, and the guide covers the entire bowl. Right now, in the dark, it shows fist-sized monsters called Night Frights emerging from the sand dunes everywhere, mobs that run at their prey, attach themselves and explode, like the rot stickers of the first floor.
beats.gist: The party's field guide shows every mob in the bowl, including exploding Night Frights.
